title: Corner C2.2 - Pixel Art Integration + Visual Polish
summary: Bridge between C2.1 (SVG approximations) and C3 (Living Office). Integrates 77 generated pixel art assets, fixes visual gaps, polishes the isometric game to the point where Patrik says 'that's it.'
content:
Corner C2.2: Pixel Art Integration + Visual Polish

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby. This is the spec that makes the game dashboard look real instead of approximated. Every task here has a generated asset to back it up.

C2.2 Mission

C2.1 proved the architecture works. The grid renders, rooms have furniture, chat connects, HUD operates. But everything is SVG approximation. The game looks like a prototype, not a product.

C2.2 swaps SVG placeholders with actual pixel art, fixes visual inconsistencies, and polishes until a non-technical person says "that looks like a real game."

Bobby's only job in C2.2: Make it look like the full-office-overhead.png render. That image IS the target.

Priority 1: Sprite Integration (Biggest Visual Win)

1A. Agent Character Swap

Replace SVG agent characters with generated sprite PNGs.

Asset paths:

projects/steffen/sprites/{agent}-idle.png
projects/steffen/sprites/{agent}-thinking.png
projects/steffen/sprites/{agent}-speaking.png
projects/steffen/sprites/{agent}-done.png

Implementation:

  • Copy all sprite PNGs to public/corner/sprites/ in aom-studio
  • In GameDashboard.jsx or a new AgentSprite component: render <img> tags instead of SVG paths
  • Default state: idle. Swap src attribute when agent state changes.
  • Size: Scale to fit within the room. At overview zoom (0.5x), sprites should be ~24-32px tall. At floor zoom (1.0x), ~48-64px. At room zoom (2.0x), ~96-128px.
  • Position: Center-bottom of each room, slightly in front of the desk (where the chair is).

State mapping:

const spriteState = (agentStatus) => {
  switch(agentStatus) {
    case 'active':   return 'thinking';   // working on something
    case 'speaking': return 'speaking';   // responding in chat
    case 'done':     return 'done';       // just finished (hold 3s then return to idle)
    default:         return 'idle';
  }
};

Animation note: The sprite sheets are multi-frame strips. For V1, just show the first frame (the static pose) of each state. Frame-by-frame animation is a C3 feature. The state swap alone is a huge upgrade.

1B. Agent Avatar in Chat

Use the idle sprite (first frame / the full image) as the agent avatar in the chat panel. Currently using colored circles. Replace with:

  • 32px square, cropped/scaled from the sprite idle image
  • Round with border-radius: 50% and 2px agentColor border
  • This makes each agent recognizable in chat without reading the name

1C. Agent Avatar in HUD Task Cards

Same approach for the task HUD. Each task card currently has a colored dot. Add a tiny (20px) sprite avatar next to it. Use the idle sprite.

Priority 2: Room Background Upgrade

2A. Room Render Backgrounds

Replace the flat-colored rectangles (floor tiles with SVG furniture) with the generated room renders as background images.

Asset paths:

projects/steffen/rooms/patrik-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/mom-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/bobby-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/elon-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/steffen-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/cleo-room.png
projects/steffen/rooms/main-hall.png

Implementation options (Bobby decides based on performance):

Option A (Recommended): Room renders as room backgrounds

  • Each room div gets background-image: url(/corner/rooms/{id}-room.png)
  • background-size: cover
  • SVG furniture STAYS as the interactive layer on top (it's already working and positioned)
  • This gives the detailed pixel art background with functional furniture overlay
  • Pros: Best of both worlds. Background provides atmosphere, SVG provides interactivity.
  • Cons: Two visual layers might look odd if alignment is off.

Option B: Full room render replacement

  • Each room renders ONLY the room background PNG
  • Remove SVG furniture entirely
  • Agent sprite overlays on top of the room image
  • Pros: Simplest, most visually cohesive.
  • Cons: Loses interactive furniture animations (server rack blinks, etc).

Option C: Selective swap

  • Use room renders for rooms WITHOUT animated furniture (Patrik, Alex, Steve, Jacob, Colton)
  • Keep SVG for rooms WITH animations (Bobby purple LEDs, Elon server blinks, Cleo waveform)
  • Balance between visual quality and animation retention

My recommendation: Start with Option B. The room renders already include all the furniture in the correct positions and style. The SVG furniture was built from text descriptions. The renders are the real thing. The interactive furniture animations (server blinks, purple LED breathing) can be overlaid as simple CSS effects on top of the static room images.

2B. Full Office Overhead as Default View

At the overview zoom level (0.5x or lower), consider using full-office-overhead.png as a single background image for the entire office, with agent status dots and nameplates overlaid. When the user zooms in, transition to individual room renders.

This gives the "wow moment" when someone first loads the dashboard. They see the full isometric office as one beautiful image. Then it becomes interactive as they zoom.

2C. Rooms Not Yet Rendered

7 rooms don't have individual renders yet: Alex, Steve, Colton, Jacob, Tony, Elmo, Pixel. For these:

  • Use the existing SVG furniture rendering (it works)
  • Or generate them: python3 scripts/generate-c2-assets.py rooms [name]-room
  • I'll add these room prompts to the generation script and run them if Bobby needs them before C3

Priority 3: Furniture Sprite Overlay

3A. Furniture PNGs as Sprites

For rooms using Option B (room renders as background), add interactive furniture overlays using the individual furniture PNGs.

Asset paths:

projects/steffen/furniture/{item-id}.png

When to use furniture PNGs:

  • Server rack LED animations (overlay on Elon's room)
  • Coffee mug steam (overlay on Patrik's/Alex's room)
  • Monitor screen flicker (overlay on any desk)
  • Any furniture item the user hovers for a tooltip

Sizing: Each furniture PNG was generated at a larger canvas (around 512x512). Bobby scales down to fit the room grid. Items should be approximately:

  • Desk: 40-48px wide in room view
  • Monitor: 16-20px wide
  • Chair: 12-16px wide
  • Server rack: 12-16px wide, 30-40px tall
  • Couch: 36-48px wide

3B. Furniture Tooltip on Hover (Nice to Have)

When hovering a room, show a tooltip with the key furniture items. Use the furniture PNGs as tiny icons in the tooltip.

Priority 4: Visual Polish

4A. Bobby's Purple LED Fix

Bobby's room had purple LED underglow in C2 but it was lost in C2.1 refactor. Add it back:

  • CSS box-shadow on Bobby's room: inset 0 0 20px rgba(156, 39, 176, 0.3)
  • Or a gradient overlay at the bottom edge of the room
  • The bobby-room.png render shows the correct look (purple glow from LED strip)

4B. Room Lighting Personality

Each room has a distinct light color (from c2-grid-spec.json). Apply a subtle CSS overlay per room:

  • Patrik: warm gold rgba(255, 216, 122, 0.05)
  • Bobby: purple rgba(156, 39, 176, 0.08)
  • Elon: cool blue-green rgba(76, 175, 80, 0.05)
  • Cleo: warm orange rgba(255, 183, 77, 0.06)
  • Steffen: golden rgba(255, 216, 122, 0.07)
  • Main Hall: warm amber rgba(255, 183, 77, 0.04)
  • Elmo: clinical white rgba(240, 240, 240, 0.06)

This is subtle but it makes rooms feel distinct even at overview zoom.

4C. Nameplate Agent Avatar

Add the tiny idle sprite (16px) next to each room's nameplate. Currently it's just text + status dot. With the sprite, you can see who lives in each room at a glance.

4D. Active Room Brightness Differential

Currently: inactive rooms at 70%, active at 100%. This needs to be more dramatic.

New spec:

  • Inactive/idle: 40% brightness (rooms feel "dark" / "sleeping")
  • Active (agent working): 100% brightness + agent color glow border (existing)
  • Speaking (agent in chat): 100% brightness + speech bubble indicator visible above room
  • Done (just finished): 100% brightness for 3s, then fade to idle

The contrast between dark idle rooms and bright active rooms should be immediately obvious. The eye goes to where the action is.

4E. CORNER Sign at Entrance

The floor plan has a "CORNER" sign at the bottom entrance. Add it to the game view:

  • Position: Below the bottom row of rooms, centered
  • Font: Syne ExtraBold 14px
  • Color: #FDF6EC on #1A1A17 background
  • Small awning shape above the text

Priority 5: Performance

5A. Sprite Preloading

Preload all idle sprites on page load. Don't preload thinking/speaking/done until an agent enters that state (lazy load).

// On mount: preload idle sprites
const agents = ['patrik','mom','alex','steve','steffen','bobby','colton','cleo','tony','jacob','elmo','elon'];
agents.forEach(a => {
  const img = new Image();
  img.src = `/corner/sprites/${a}-idle.png`;
});

5B. Room Image Optimization

The room PNGs are 1.1-1.5MB each. Before deploying to Vercel:

  • Convert to WebP (60-70% smaller, same quality)
  • Or use Next.js Image optimization if available
  • Or use Gumlet/Cloudinary CDN (Bobby already uses Gumlet for Ambition)

Target: Each room image under 200KB. Full office overhead under 400KB.

5C. Sprite Sheet Optimization

The sprite sheets are also 1MB+ each. For the static "first frame only" approach in C2.2:

  • Crop to just the first frame of each state (reduces size by 75-87%)
  • Or create a CSS sprite approach with background-position offsets
  • This is prep work for C3's frame-by-frame animation anyway

What Bobby Delivers in C2.2

Checkboxes Bobby can burn down:

  • Copy sprite PNGs to public/corner/sprites/
  • Copy furniture PNGs to public/corner/furniture/
  • Copy room PNGs to public/corner/rooms/
  • Swap SVG agent characters with sprite idle PNGs
  • Add agent state -> sprite state mapping (idle/thinking/speaking/done)
  • Replace colored circles in chat with sprite avatars
  • Room backgrounds: implement Option A, B, or C (Bobby's call)
  • Fix Bobby's purple LED glow
  • Add per-room lighting color overlay
  • Increase inactive room dimming (70% -> 40%)
  • Add CORNER entrance sign
  • Optimize images for production (WebP or CDN)
  • Preload idle sprites on mount

Nice to have (if time allows):

  • Full office overhead as default overview image
  • Furniture PNG overlays for interactive elements
  • Nameplate sprite avatars
  • Hover tooltips with furniture icons

After C2.2

Once the game dashboard looks like the full-office-overhead.png render, we're ready for C3: The Living Office. C3 adds the "feel" layer (WebSocket real-time, character movement, mode switching, mobile). But C2.2 is the visual foundation. If the game doesn't LOOK right, no amount of real-time features will matter.

C2.2 success metric: Someone sees the dashboard and says "wait, is that a game?" before they realize it's a business tool.

77 assets generated. Zero excuses for SVG placeholders. Make it pixel perfect, Bobby.
